pending_commit.commit_message: login: Force crashpad on kukui Force kukui devices to start using crashpad immediately. Breakpad does not work on kukui devices such as Krane. We are losing crash reports from Chrome browser processes, and other Chrome crash reports are corrupt and unusable. This is a launch blocker for Krane; we don't know if there are stability issues. Crashpad does not have the same issues as breakpad on these devices. We want to move to crashpad eventually anyways, so rather than trying to fix the deprecated breakpad, let's move to crashpad on kukui. There are no released kukui devices, so this only affects testers. Other devices do not have the same issues with breakpad, so we can do a slower rollout & dogfooding for everything else in later CLs. This is just the emergency switchover for kukui. BUG=chromium:1001139 TEST=On a Krane. kill -SEGV main chrome process. Visit chrome://crash, chrome://gpucrash, and chrome://inducebrowsercrashforrealz. All produce crash reports. FROMLIST: tracing: Fix possible double free on failure of allocating trace buffer commit 4397f04575c44e1440ec2e49b6302785c95fd2f8 upstream. Jing Xia and Chunyan Zhang reported that on failing to allocate part of the tracing buffer, memory is freed, but the pointers that point to them are not initialized back to NULL, and later paths may try to free the freed memory again. Jing and Chunyan fixed one of the locations that does this, but missed a spot. Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20171226071253.8968-1-chunyan.zhang@spreadtrum.com BUG=chromium:1003316 TEST=None Change-Id: I7b719a7bb6d3ed779807a6179ce28aefb14816fa Fixes: 737223fbca3b1 ("tracing: Consolidate buffer allocation code") Reported-by: Jing Xia <jing.xia@spreadtrum.com> Reported-by: Chunyan Zhang <chunyan.zhang@spreadtrum.com> Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (VMware) <rostedt@goodmis.org> Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> (cherry picked from commit f9e16c238bd6da1d858d50c1ab81c8431578877a from linux-3.18.y) Signed-off-by: Zubin Mithra <zsm@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1800481 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>

init: fix incorrect result from GetBlockCount The GetBlockCount helper function falls back to checking /sys/class/block/[dev]/size to get a count of blocks if dumpe2fs fails. However, that interface returns a count of sectors (512 bytes) instead of blocks (often 4096 bytes). This means that if we do get the block count from this fallback, our count will be 8 times too large. This causes an error message when we attempt to write beyond the size of the file system. Add block size as a parameter to GetBlockCount, so that we can convert the sector count into a block count. BUG=None TEST=None Change-Id: I6fde163d8553e36ddddda02a0f244c409eb1ccc9 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1834428 Tested-by: Fletcher Woodruff <fletcherw@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Fletcher Woodruff <fletcherw@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

touch_updater: Fix uses of "shift" that may unintentionally exit. POSIX allows, but does not require, "shift" to exit a non-interactive shell on failure. Both the ambiguity and the exit are unfortunate. We must work around it by assuming any use of "shift" might exit the shell unless we have already tested that there are sufficient args left for it to succeed. I am unsure why I did not catch this when testing the 1 arg form of rebind_driver() as part of CL:1772378 verification. I examined the logs but perhaps I glossed over them too quickly, since that particular touch device generally works without a rebind after reflash. BUG=b:132830741,b:139569213 TEST=Tested etphidiap, st-touch, and raydium updaters on their respective devices. Tested no-update, yes-update, and corrupt-fw-recovery scenarios for each. Of note, this includes coverage of rebind_driver() with 1 arg (raydium) and 2 args (etphidiap, st-touch). Change-Id: Ia7b73e7a2014a07bfe6597c4322ffa20a09960ae Signed-off-by: Matthew Blecker <matthewb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1832412 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Harry Cutts <hcutts@chromium.org>
